newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks lifted higher in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks lifted higher in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks bounced back on Wednesday morning with institutional investors picking up bargains in a few key index stocks following Wall Street's modest rebound, brokers said.
"We are seeing an element of bargain hunting today," said Julian Ings Chambers at BZW Securities Asia.
The Hang Seng Index was trading 19 points, or 0.16 percent higher at 12,093 after leaping more than 100 points at the open. Turnover was a robust HK$1.55 billion.
The Dow closed 27.57 points higher at 6,611.05 overnight, but brokers said market breadth was not very positive.
Institutions were seeking bargains among the index constituents, buying in HSBC Holdings,, Hang Seng Bank , and Cheung Kong.

The finance sector led the blue chips, followed by utilities. HSBC Holdings added HK$1.00 to HK$176.00 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.50 to HK$76.75. Hongkong Telecom put on HK$0.05 to HK$12.80 before easing to trade unchanged at HK$12.75.

"I wouldn't bottom fish yet. We may have another 200 to 300 points down yet," said Alistair Candlish, head of derivatives trading at W.I.Carr.Property developers were mixed. Cheung Kong advanced HK$0.50 to HK$64.25, while Sun Hung Kai Properties shed HK$1.00 to HK$77.50.
H shares remained under pressure, while mid caps outperformed most other market sectors. Tsingtao Brewery added HK$0.05 to HK$3.05, but Qingling Motors lost HK$0.07 to HK$3.90.
Red chip mid cap China Resources was trading HK$0.15 higher at HK$16.30 and Dah Sing Financial gained HK$0.20 to HK$29.50.
Hang Seng Index futures opened at a discount of more than 100 points to the cash market, signalling caution on the longer term view.
"There is some index arbitrage activity, but it is limited compared with yesterday," said Candlish.
The April contract opened at 12,040, then eased to trade 62 points higher at 12,032.
